# Andika Dwi Saputra (andikadevs): full profile

> Fullstack developer in Semarang, Indonesia, open to remote roles. This file is the complete text of https://andikadevs.github.io/ in plain Markdown. An Indonesian version of the site is at https://andikadevs.github.io/?lang=id.

## About

I build the software companies quietly run on: internal tools, single sign-on, media services, AI pipelines. Three-plus years, mostly for universities and hiring platforms in Indonesia.

I started as an intern at a Toyota dealership, writing Laravel. Today I run the platform behind a university's apps, build tools for Toploker.com, and keep a small studio going on the side. I like problems where a boring manual step is costing someone hours a week.

Built for: Universitas STEKOM, Toploker.com, Akastra Toyota, Kerja Malam, Digitek.

## Case studies

### STEKOM International

- Category: University website
- Client: Universitas STEKOM
- Year: 2026
- Link: https://international.stekom.ac.id 
- Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, Bun, MySQL, Drizzle ORM, NextAuth, S3
- Areas: Web, Backend

The official international site of Universitas STEKOM. Real English and Indonesian pages, plus an admin where each department runs its own content.

**The problem.** Two audiences that rarely overlap: partners and students abroad reading English, and people at home reading Indonesian. Several departments edit the site, so one shared admin password was never going to work.

**What I did.** Locale-aware routing so every page has a proper EN and ID version. Role-based access through NextAuth, so each department only touches its own news, agendas and partner data. News is pulled from the existing campus portal API instead of being typed in twice.

**Results.** EN / ID (Bilingual, i18n routing); RBAC (Per-department admin).

### STEKOM Passport

- Category: Identity & SSO
- Client: Universitas STEKOM
- Year: 2026
- Link: https://passport.stekom.ac.id 
- Stack: NestJS 11, Bun, React 19, PostgreSQL, Redis, Socket.IO
- Areas: Backend, API, DevOps

An OpenID Connect provider for the whole campus. One login for every internal app, with typed SDKs for TypeScript, Python and PHP.

**The problem.** Every new internal system came with its own user table and its own password reset. When someone left, their accounts were scattered across apps nobody remembered.

**What I did.** Authorization Code with PKCE, ID-token verification, and both RP-initiated and back-channel logout, so logging out once really ends the session everywhere. The SDKs mean another team can plug in an existing app in an afternoon.

**Results.** 11+ (Apps on single sign-on); 3 SDKs (TypeScript, Python, PHP).

### OTO Management

- Category: Internal system
- Client: Toploker.com
- Year: 2024
- Link: https://andikadevs.github.io/#project/oto-management (internal system, not public)
- Stack: Next.js, Laravel 11, MySQL, Redis, WebSockets, Docker
- Areas: Backend, Web, Automation

Toploker's operational backbone: ads, revenue recaps, invoices and broadcasts in one place, updating live.

**The problem.** Marketing, finance and file management each lived in a different tool. Data didn't line up, people re-typed the same numbers, and decisions waited on someone's spreadsheet.

**What I did.** A Next.js front end on a Laravel API, with WebSockets pushing changes to everyone who has the page open. Broadcasts and heavy jobs run on Redis queues so the app never stalls, and assets come straight from Google Drive.

**Results.** 20+ h (Manual work saved monthly); Live (WebSocket updates).

### SnapCRM

- Category: WhatsApp automation
- Client: Universitas STEKOM & Toploker.com
- Year: 2024
- Link: https://andikadevs.github.io/#project/snapcrm (internal system, not public)
- Stack: Node.js, Laravel, TypeScript, MySQL, Docker
- Areas: Automation, Backend, API

A CRM that turns large lead lists into WhatsApp conversations, with broadcasts and auto-reply flows.

**The problem.** Marketing had hundreds of thousands of leads and no realistic way to follow up by hand. Existing tools didn't do the WhatsApp side properly.

**What I did.** Node.js and Laravel talking to the WhatsApp HTTP API, a broadcast engine that paces itself, and reply flows that handle the common questions so people only step in when it matters.

**Results.** 100K+ (Leads managed); 100K+ (Broadcasts delivered).

### Corpus

- Category: AI research pipeline
- Client: Universitas STEKOM
- Year: 2026
- Link: https://andikadevs.github.io/#project/corpus (internal system, not public)
- Stack: NestJS 11, Bun, React 19, PostgreSQL, DeepSeek, Zotero API, Pandoc
- Areas: AI, Backend

A multi-agent pipeline that drafts academic manuscripts from real sources, and refuses to ship a citation it can't trace back.

**The problem.** Getting a model to write text is easy. Getting citations that exist and actually support the sentence they're attached to is the hard part. General chatbots invent references without blinking.

**What I did.** Seven stages from retrieval to formatted output, ending in an integrity gate. Sources get stable short refs so citations are parsed straight from the model's markers. Researchers can ground drafts in their own Zotero library.

**Results.** 7 (Pipeline stages); 6 (Citation styles).

### Kerja Malam

- Category: Job portal · PWA
- Client: Kerja Malam
- Year: 2025
- Link: https://kerjamalam.com 
- Stack: React 19, TanStack Start, Vite, Bun, Tailwind CSS 4, Zod
- Areas: Web

A job board for night-shift, part-time and freelance work in Indonesia. Light enough for a cheap phone, and it still works offline.

**The problem.** The people looking for this work are on mid-range Android phones with patchy data. Most job boards are too heavy to load, and lose the listing you were reading the moment the signal drops.

**What I did.** A small JavaScript payload on TanStack Start, search filters kept in the URL so results survive a refresh and can be shared, and a full PWA so saved listings stay readable offline.

**Results.** PWA (Installable, works offline); 4 (Filters at once).

### Depot

- Category: Media service
- Client: Universitas STEKOM
- Year: 2026
- Link: https://depot.stekom.ac.id 
- Stack: NestJS 11, Bun, PostgreSQL, Redis, BullMQ, S3
- Areas: Backend, API, DevOps

One multi-tenant media service for every campus app: presigned uploads, background thumbnails and transcodes, signed delivery, HMAC webhooks.

**The problem.** Each app had rebuilt file handling its own way. Big uploads streamed through app servers, access rules didn't match, and nobody knew how much storage anything used.

**What I did.** The client gets a presigned URL and uploads straight to S3, so no large file passes through the API. Processing runs on BullMQ, and short-lived signed URLs mean access can be revoked without moving anything.

**Results.** 0 bytes (Through the API on upload); 3 SDKs (TypeScript, Python, PHP).

### PDDikti API & MCP

- Category: Open-source API
- Client: Open source
- Year: 2026
- Link: https://github.com/andikadevs/pddikti 
- Stack: Bun, Hono, TypeScript, Zod, OpenAPI, MCP
- Areas: API, AI

A typed, documented read-only API over Indonesia's higher-education dataset, also exposed as an MCP server so AI agents can query it.

**The problem.** PDDikti is the source of truth for campuses, programmes and lecturers, but it sits behind Cloudflare with undocumented responses. Every team ends up writing the same fragile scraper.

**What I did.** Each endpoint is defined once as a Zod schema, which generates both the validation and the OpenAPI docs, so they can't drift apart. The same surface is served as MCP tools.

**Results.** OpenAPI (Docs generated from schema); MCP (Usable by AI agents).

### Jobs Scraper

- Category: AI data pipeline
- Client: Toploker.com
- Year: 2026
- Link: https://andikadevs.github.io/#project/jobs-scraper (internal system, not public)
- Stack: Bun, React 19, PostgreSQL, Puppeteer, Gemini, WebSocket
- Areas: Automation, AI, Backend

Watches Instagram accounts by region, scrapes vacancy posts, and lets Gemini sort real jobs from noise before anything hits the database.

**The problem.** A lot of Indonesian vacancies are just an Instagram post with a WhatsApp number. The same accounts mix jobs with promos and reposts, and scrapers break without telling you why.

**What I did.** Puppeteer on a schedule, Gemini classification, Zod validation on every record, and a dashboard that streams each run's logs live, so a failed run can actually be explained.

**Results.** Gemini (Post classification); Live (Per-run logs).

### Conflow

- Category: Content scheduling
- Client: Universitas STEKOM
- Year: 2026
- Link: https://conflow.stekom.ac.id 
- Stack: NestJS 11, Bun, React 19, PostgreSQL, Redis, Google Drive API
- Areas: Web, Backend, Automation

Write, schedule and publish social posts across channels from one dashboard, with a media library that imports from Google Drive.

**The problem.** Campus content was run through group chats and spreadsheets. Whoever had the password posted it, usually late, and nobody could say what was going out next week.

**What I did.** Posts are written once and queued for their time slot, so nothing depends on someone being awake. Roles separate drafting from publishing, and a calendar answers the “what's next week” question.

**Results.** Queue (Scheduled publishing); Drive (Import into media library).

### Bio

- Category: Link-in-bio builder
- Client: Universitas STEKOM
- Year: 2026
- Link: https://bio.stekom.ac.id 
- Stack: Laravel, Octane, Inertia, React 19, MySQL, Tailwind CSS 4
- Areas: Web, Backend

A self-hosted link-in-bio builder for campus teams: drag-and-drop pages, themes, QR codes and analytics that stay on campus servers.

**The problem.** Departments and student groups were each paying for a hosted account, or sharing one. Analytics were scattered and the branding was all over the place.

**What I did.** Laravel with Octane and Inertia, so it feels like an SPA but deploys as one app. Themed presets give every team an on-brand page without needing a designer.

**Results.** Teams (Separate workspaces); 0 (SaaS fees).

### TopMatch

- Category: HR SaaS landing
- Client: Toploker.com
- Year: 2025
- Link: https://match.toploker.com 
- Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Lenis
- Areas: Web

The recruitment product site for Toploker, aimed at HR teams, with pricing out in the open.

**The problem.** Toploker's usual audience is job seekers. TopMatch sells to hiring managers, who want to know what it does, what it costs and who uses it, fast.

**What I did.** One page built around one decision: value, services, plans, call to action. Motion guides the eye through pricing instead of decorating it, and it's statically generated so ads land on a fast page.

**Results.** Static (Fast for paid traffic); Open (Published pricing).
